title: Share equally among trays: find how many on each

beats.say: Three trays, with five counters on each tray. How many counters are there in all?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: There are 3 trays with 5 counters on each tray. How many counters are there in all?

beats.say: A tray holds counters. Every tray here has the same number of counters, so these are equal groups.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Count the counters by fives, one tray at a time.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five, ten, fifteen.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Three trays times five on each tray makes fifteen counters in all.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Equal groups have three numbers: the trays, the number on each tray, and the total.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Here the total was the missing number, so we multiplied.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Next, the total is known, and the number on each tray is missing.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Share eight counters equally among four trays. How many counters belong on each tray?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Share 8 counters equally among 4 trays. How many counters belong on each tray?

beats.say: The counters waiting to be shared are the pile. Sharing equally means every tray gets the same number, and none stay in the pile.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: Every tray gets the same number of counters, and none are left in the pile.

beats.say: Four trays, eight counters. I multiplied last time, so four times eight: thirty-two on each tray?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Four times eight is four trays with eight on each tray, thirty-two counters in all.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Test it on the figure. This pile has only eight counters. Put the whole pile on the first tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The pile is empty, and that one tray holds eight. The other three trays have none.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: So thirty-two on each tray is impossible. Nobody can get more than the pile has: eight.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Put the counters back.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four trays share the pile, so each tray gets only part of it. Multiplying the pile by the trays makes a number bigger than the pile.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: The total is given, and each tray gets only part of it. Do not multiply the total by the trays.

beats.say: Now share equally. Deal one counter to each tray, in turn: the first tray, the second, the third, the fourth.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: That is one round: one counter on every tray. A round uses four counters, one for each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Every tray has one, so the trays match. But four are still in the pile.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Deal another round, until the pile is empty.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The pile is empty. Every tray has two counters, the same number.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Each round gave every tray one counter, so the number of rounds is the number on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Write it as a multiplication: four trays times the number on each tray makes eight.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The box stands for the number we do not know yet: the number on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Four times two makes eight, so the deal found the box: two.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two counters belong on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Share thirty counters equally among six trays. How many counters belong on each tray?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Share 30 counters equally among 6 trays. How many counters belong on each tray?

beats.say: Dealing one counter at a time would take thirty moves.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Deal a round at a time. How many counters does one round use?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Six. A round puts one counter on every tray, and there are six trays.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Round one: six counters dealt, twenty-four left.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Round two: twelve dealt, eighteen left.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Round three: eighteen dealt, twelve left. Each round adds six, so I am counting by sixes.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Keep counting by sixes until the pile is empty: twenty-four, thirty.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five rounds, and the pile is empty. How many counters does each tray have?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Every round gave each tray one counter. Five rounds, so five on each tray.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Write it as a multiplication: six trays times the box makes thirty.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The box is how many sixes make thirty. Counting by sixes found it: five.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Count by the number of trays until you reach the total.

beats.say: Finding the box is called division. Thirty divided by six.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.meaning: Splitting a total into equal shares to find the size of each share. $30 \div 6$ is read thirty divided by six.

beats.say: So thirty divided by six means thirty counters shared among six trays?
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Yes. The total goes first, then the number of trays. The answer is how many each tray gets.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check by multiplying back: six trays with five on each tray make thirty.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Five counters belong on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Share twenty-four counters equally among three trays. How many counters belong on each tray?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Share 24 counters equally among 3 trays. How many counters belong on each tray?

beats.say: Before dealing, say the division for this pile and these trays.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Trays came first in the multiplication, so trays first here: three divided by twenty-four.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: A division starts with what is being shared. Here the pile is shared: twenty-four counters.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: In a division, the total goes first. It is the number that gets shared.

beats.say: Three divided by twenty-four would share three counters among twenty-four trays. This figure has twenty-four counters and three trays.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Twenty-four divided by three. Twenty-four counters shared among three trays.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Now find the box. Write the multiplication: three trays times the box makes twenty-four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: How many counters does a round use? Count by that number as you deal.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three, one for each tray. So: three, six, nine, twelve, fifteen, eighteen, twenty-one, twenty-four.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Eight rounds, and the pile is empty. What does the number of rounds tell us?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Each round gave every tray one counter, so each tray has eight. Twenty-four divided by three is eight.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Check by multiplying back: three trays with eight on each tray make twenty-four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eight counters belong on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Share twenty-four counters equally among eight trays. How many counters belong on each tray?
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Share 24 counters equally among 8 trays. How many counters belong on each tray?

beats.say: The same twenty-four counters, now on eight trays instead of three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Last time, each of three trays got eight. The dashed line marks eight on a tray. Will each of eight trays get more than eight, or fewer?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eight trays is more trays, so more counters on each. Past the dashed line.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Test it. A round puts one counter on each of eight trays, so a round uses eight counters.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Round one: eight dealt, sixteen left.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Round two: sixteen dealt, eight left.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Round three: twenty-four dealt, none left.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The pile ran out after three rounds, so each tray has three.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Three trays gave eight each, up to the dashed line. Eight trays give three each, far short of it. More trays, smaller shares.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: The same pile is cut into more shares, so each share is smaller.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Same total, more trays: each tray gets fewer counters.

beats.say: Write the multiplication: eight trays times the box makes twenty-four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Twenty-four divided by eight is three.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Check by multiplying back: eight trays with three on each tray make twenty-four.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Three counters belong on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Share fifty-six counters equally among eight trays. How many counters belong on each tray? Champ, work this one.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Share 56 counters equally among 8 trays. How many counters belong on each tray?

beats.say: Which of the three numbers is missing: trays, each, or total?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Trays: eight. Total: fifty-six, the pile. The number on each tray is missing.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Write what you know as trays times box.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eight times box equals fifty-six.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Now find the box with the figure. How many counters does one round use?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eight, one for each tray.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: So I count by eights until I reach fifty-six, one round for each count: eight, sixteen, twenty-four, thirty-two, forty, forty-eight, fifty-six.
beats.speaker: learner

do.text: Count by the number of trays until you reach the total.

beats.say: How many counts did you make?
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Seven rounds, so seven on each tray.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Now write the division for this pile and these trays.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The pile is shared among the trays, so the pile goes first. Fifty-six divided by eight is seven.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Check it by multiplying back.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Eight trays with seven on each tray is eight times seven, fifty-six. That matches the pile.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Now say why counting rounds finds the number on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: The pile is the total. Each round gives every tray one counter, so it uses eight, one for each tray. The pile is empty after seven rounds, so each tray has seven.
beats.speaker: learner

beats.say: Seven counters belong on each tray.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Every shared pile goes the same way.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: One. Name the three numbers: trays, each, and total.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Two. Write trays times box equals total.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Write trays times box equals total.

beats.say: Three. Count by the number of trays until you reach the total.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Count by the trays up to the total. The number of counts is the number on each tray.

beats.say: Four. Divide, total first. Then check by multiplying back.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Divide, total first. Check by multiplying back.

beats.say: Five. Know the multiplication fact, and you can skip the dealing.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Know the fact, skip the dealing: $8 \times 7 = 56$, so $56 \div 8 = 7$.
